name: Swelling-alarm cast
subtitle: a cast that warns before swelling crushes muscle

effects.effect: pressure on a confined liquid is passed on equally everywhere

effect: pressure on a confined liquid is passed on equally everywhere
how: After a broken leg, swelling inside a tight cast can choke the muscles (compartment syndrome) and cost the limb within hours, and the only warning is pain that sedated patients and small children can't report. A thin liner of linked, fluid-filled pockets sits under the cast; swelling anywhere squeezes it, the pressure spreads equally through the whole liner (Pascal's law), and one gauge at its edge sounds an alarm.
obstacle: Pressure on the skin under a cast tracks the pressure inside the muscle only loosely, so the alarm threshold is hard to set.
why: Turns a silent, limb-threatening emergency into an alarm for patients who can't say it hurts.
real: Patents describe fluid-filled bladders/capsules under casts linked to a pressure sensor or indicator with an alarm for excessive pressure (e.g. US 4858620), and a 2022 study tested an under-cast Bluetooth pressure sensor; no product found.
